title: The Quiet Hero of the Flood
summary: A quiet, often-overlooked boy notices rising floodwater near an elderly neighbor's house before anyone else does, and his quick, calm warning helps the whole family reach safety in time.
poll: The people who help the most are usually the loudest, most noticeable people in a group.

versions.title: The Quiet Hero of the Flood
versions.text:
The sky grew dark. It rained hard. The water rose fast. This was a flood.

Rami sat by the window. He was quiet. He liked to notice things. He saw it rise.

Rami told his mom. He told his dad. They looked outside. It was near a house. The house was their neighbor Hamad's.

Dad ran to warn him. Hamad lives alone. He is old. The family helped him grab his things.

They all went to high ground. The water rose high. But everyone was safe.

By morning, the flood went down. The street was safe again. Hamad said thanks to Rami. Rami did not brag at all.

versions.title: The Quiet Hero of the Flood
versions.text:
The sky had been dark for hours. Then it started to rain hard. Soon the water in the street began to rise.

Rami liked to sit by his window. He was a quiet boy. He liked to notice small things. That evening, he noticed something odd. The water was rising fast.

Rami ran to tell his mom and dad. They looked outside. They saw that he was right. The water had crept close to a house. It was their neighbor's house. Their neighbor was an old man named Hamad. He lived alone next door.

Dad rushed over to warn Hamad about the flood. Hamad was surprised. But he trusted them right away. The family helped him get a few things fast.

Together, they all walked to higher ground. They got there before the water reached Hamad's door. The flood rose high in the street that night. But everyone stayed safe.

By morning, the flood water had gone down. The street was muddy but safe again. Hamad thanked Rami. Rami just smiled. He was glad he had been watching.

The sky had been dark and heavy for hours. Then the rain began to fall hard. Soon the water in the narrow street started to rise.

Rami liked to sit quietly by his window every evening. He was a quiet boy. He noticed small things that other people often missed. That evening, he noticed something strange. The water outside was rising fast. It was rising much faster than it usually did after rain.

Rami ran to tell his mom and dad right away. They looked outside. They quickly saw that he was right. The rising water had crept close to their neighbor's small house. Their neighbor was an old man named Hamad. He lived alone next door. He rarely left his home.

Rami's dad rushed over at once. He wanted to warn Hamad about the flood. Hamad was startled. But he trusted the family right away. Together, they helped him gather a few important things.

Everyone then walked together to higher ground. They reached safety just in time. The water had not yet reached Hamad's front door. The flood rose dangerously high in the street that night. Yet everyone stayed completely safe.

By morning, the flood water had finally gone down. The street was muddy and messy. But it was safe once again. Hamad warmly thanked Rami for noticing the danger so early. Rami simply smiled. He was glad that he had been paying attention.

versions.title: The Quiet Hero of the Flood
versions.text:
Imagine noticing something important that everyone else has completely missed. That is exactly what happened to a quiet boy named Rami. It happened one stormy evening in his small village.

For hours, dark clouds had been gathering over the hills. Then heavy rain finally began to fall. Rami was sitting quietly by his window, as he often did. Most people overlooked Rami because he rarely spoke up in a crowd. But he was remarkably observant. That evening, he noticed the water in the street rising fast. It was rising far faster than usual.

Rami rushed to alert his parents right away. His mother and father looked outside. They immediately saw that he was right. The rising water had already crept close to a neighbor's home. Their neighbor was an elderly man named Hamad. He lived alone and rarely left his house.

Rami's father hurried over to warn Hamad about the flood. He wanted to warn him before the water reached his door. Hamad was startled. But he trusted the family and acted quickly. Together, they helped him gather a few essential things. They moved with calm but cautious speed.

The whole group then walked briskly to higher ground. They reached safety just moments before the water arrived. The flood rose dangerously high in the street that night. Yet everyone remained completely safe.

By morning, the flood water had slowly receded. Hamad thanked Rami warmly for being so alert. The quiet boy simply smiled. He was happy that his careful attention had made such a difference.

versions.title: The Quiet Hero of the Flood
versions.text:
In the small village of Salam, a boy named Rami possessed a quality that almost nobody around him ever noticed: quiet vigilance, the habit of paying close attention while saying very little. On one particularly tumultuous evening, as dark clouds gathered ominously over the surrounding hills and torrential rain began to fall around sunset, Rami sat quietly by his bedroom window, as was his customary habit, and noticed something that everyone else in his household had entirely missed: the water in the street outside was rising with unusual, almost alarming speed, considerably faster than it typically did after an ordinary, unremarkable rain.

Rami's quiet, unassuming nature meant that people often overlooked him entirely, especially beside his louder, more outgoing older sister, who teased him gently without ever realizing how closely and consistently he paid attention to the world around him. Yet it was precisely this overlooked, perceptive trait that proved essential that evening, as Rami rushed to alert his parents, who looked outside and recognized at once that his observation was entirely accurate: the rising water had already crept within a few meters of their elderly neighbor's modest home.

Their neighbor, an elderly man named Hamad, lived entirely alone and rarely ventured outside, even during ordinary weather, preferring the quiet seclusion of his own small courtyard, which meant that no one else in the village was likely to notice his growing danger in time. Rami's father hurried over immediately to warn him about the rapidly approaching flood, hoping desperately to reach him before the water inevitably did, and though Hamad was startled initially, he trusted the family completely and acted without hesitation, helping them gather a few essential belongings as they moved with calm yet discreet urgency through the increasingly darkening, water-logged street.

The whole group then walked briskly toward higher ground nearby, their footsteps quickening with each passing moment, and they reached safety only minutes before the rising water finally arrived at Hamad's doorstep. The flood rose dangerously high in the narrow street that night, swirling noisily past the silent, shuttered houses, yet everyone remained entirely unharmed throughout the frightening ordeal, a fact that owed almost everything to one quiet boy's careful attention.

By morning, the flood water had gradually receded, leaving the street muddy but perfectly safe once again, and Hamad offered Rami quiet commendation for his remarkable alertness, without any public fuss or fanfare whatsoever, simply a warm handshake and a few heartfelt, sincere words. The unassuming boy simply smiled, quietly content in the knowledge that paying close attention, rather than seeking recognition, had made a genuine and lasting difference to someone who needed it most.

He did not get along with any of his neighbors
He may have been elderly and preferred a quiet, simple routine
He was deeply afraid of the entire village council
questions.why: The article describes Hamad as an elderly man who lived alone and rarely left his house, suggesting a quiet daily routine.

wrong.A: The article gives no sign that Hamad planned to move.
wrong.B: Hamad trusted and welcomed the family's help.
wrong.D: The article does not mention the village council frightening him.

questions.stem: What can you tell about Rami's personality from the story?
options: He enjoys being the loud center of attention
He is careless and never notices small details
He strongly dislikes helping other people nearby
He is quiet but unusually alert and observant
questions.why: Rami is described as quiet, yet he noticed the danger before anyone else, showing he is alert and observant.

wrong.A: Rami avoids attention rather than seeking it.
wrong.B: Rami notices small details others miss.
wrong.C: Rami works hard to help his elderly neighbor.

questions.stem: Why does the author include the detail that Hamad thanked Rami quietly, without a fuss?
options: To show that meaningful recognition does not always need to be loud or public
To suggest that Hamad was actually not very grateful to Rami, and wished to say nothing
To explain the detailed official rules for thanking a rescuer in a village
To compare Hamad's house with the busy village council building near the well
questions.why: The quiet thank-you matches the story's theme that Rami's quiet attention mattered more than seeking attention.

wrong.B: Hamad's quiet thanks still showed real gratitude.
wrong.C: The article does not describe official rules.
wrong.D: The article does not compare buildings.

MID.prompt: Explain how Rami's quiet, observant personality helped save his elderly neighbor. Use at least two details from the article.
checklist: I explained how Rami's personality helped save Hamad.
I used at least two details from the article.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: Rami's quiet, observant personality was the key to saving his neighbor. Because he liked to sit quietly by his window, he noticed the water rising much faster than usual, something that busier or louder people might have missed. Being overlooked by others never stopped him from paying close attention, and that attention let him alert his parents in time. Together, the family warned Hamad and helped him reach safety before the flood reached his door.

keyWords.definition: careful and continuous attention to possible danger
keyWords.example: The night guard's vigilance helped him spot the fire before it spread.

keyWords.definition: quick to notice or understand things that are not obvious
keyWords.example: The perceptive detective noticed a clue that everyone else had missed.

keyWords.definition: modest and not seeking attention or praise
keyWords.example: The unassuming scientist let her colleagues present the discovery.

keyWords.definition: careful not to attract attention or cause a fuss
keyWords.example: He gave discreet help to his classmate without telling anyone else.

keyWords.definition: praise or formal recognition for doing something well
keyWords.example: The firefighter received a quiet commendation for her bravery.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the article?
options: A perceptive boy's quiet vigilance helps him save a neighbor
A village builds a modern warning system after a flood in the town
An elderly man ends up losing his home and moving away
A boy becomes the subject of a famous village legend
questions.why: The article centers on Rami's quiet vigilance and perceptiveness, which allow him to notice danger and help save Hamad.

wrong.B: The article does not describe a new warning system.
wrong.C: Hamad does not lose his home or move away.
wrong.D: The article does not describe a village legend.

questions.stem: According to the article, how did Rami typically spend his evenings?
options: Working at the local village market
Sitting quietly by his bedroom window
Helping his older sister with homework
Playing loudly with several neighborhood friends
questions.why: In the article, Rami habitually sat quietly by his bedroom window most evenings.

wrong.A: The article does not mention a market job.
wrong.C: The article does not mention homework.
wrong.D: The article does not describe Rami playing loudly.

questions.stem: What specific comparison does the article make between Rami and his sister?
options: Rami is older, while his sister is much younger
Rami dislikes their neighbor, while his sister admires him in their village
Rami is unassuming, while his sister is louder and more outgoing
Rami is careless, while his sister is extremely cautious
questions.why: The article contrasts Rami's unassuming, quiet nature with his sister's louder, more outgoing personality.

wrong.A: The article does not describe their relative ages.
wrong.B: Both the family and Hamad trust one another.
wrong.D: Rami, not his sister, is shown as unusually attentive.

questions.stem: Why did Rami's father act so quickly after hearing about the rising water?
options: Because the village council had already ordered an evacuation
Because Hamad had already called asking for help
Because the family had experienced this exact flood before
Because he trusted Rami's observation about the rising flood
questions.why: Rami's father believed his son's accurate observation and recognized that the flood threatened Hamad's home.

wrong.A: The article does not mention a village council order.
wrong.B: Hamad did not call; the family came to warn him.
wrong.C: The article does not mention a previous identical flood.

questions.stem: In the article, to be unassuming means to —
options: constantly seek praise and public attention
be modest and avoid drawing attention to oneself
ignore other people's problems completely
act carelessly without thinking of consequences
questions.why: Rami is described as unassuming because he avoids seeking attention, even after helping save his neighbor.

wrong.A: Unassuming means the opposite of seeking attention.
wrong.C: Rami pays close attention to others' problems.
wrong.D: Rami acts carefully, not carelessly.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the village's usual response to quiet, unassuming people like Rami?
options: They are likely often overlooked despite their skills
They are usually given leadership roles in the village council
They are excluded from community events entirely
They receive more attention than loud, outgoing people
questions.why: The article shows that people habitually overlooked Rami, implying quiet individuals often go unnoticed despite their abilities.

wrong.B: The article gives no sign Rami holds a leadership role.
wrong.C: Rami participates fully in the rescue, not excluded.
wrong.D: The opposite is suggested: quiet people receive less attention.

questions.stem: How are Rami's vigilance and Hamad's trust similar in the way they drive the story forward?
options: Both are unrelated background details with no effect on events
Both are quiet, often-overlooked qualities that directly make the rescue possible
Both are qualities that the village council specifically trained them to have
Both qualities appear only after the flood has already ended
questions.why: Rami's vigilance leads him to notice the danger, while Hamad's quick trust lets the family act before it is too late; both quiet qualities drive the rescue.

wrong.A: Both qualities directly shape how the rescue unfolds.
wrong.C: The article does not mention any formal training.
wrong.D: Both qualities appear before and during the flood, not after.

questions.stem: Why does the author end the article by emphasizing Hamad's discreet commendation rather than a public celebration?
options: To imply that Hamad was secretly embarrassed by what happened in the village
To criticize the village for not holding a public celebration for the boy
To suggest that quiet recognition can be just as meaningful as public praise
To shift the whole story's focus away from Rami and onto the elder
questions.why: The quiet commendation mirrors Rami's own unassuming nature, suggesting that meaningful recognition need not be loud or public.

wrong.A: Nothing suggests Hamad felt embarrassed.
wrong.B: The article does not criticize the village.
wrong.D: The ending keeps the focus squarely on Rami.

HIGH.prompt: The poll suggests that the people who help the most are usually the loudest, most noticeable people in a group. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the article about Rami's vigilance and his quiet commendation.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the article.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I disagree with the poll statement. In the article, Rami is an unassuming, often-overlooked boy, yet his quiet vigilance is exactly what allows him to notice the flood before anyone louder or more noticeable does. Someone might argue that loud, confident people are usually the first to act in an emergency because they draw attention and organize others quickly. However, Hamad's rescue depended entirely on Rami's perceptive, discreet attention, and the fact that Hamad offered him only a quiet commendation afterward shows that meaningful help does not require being the loudest person in the room.
